Oxford Nanopore single-nucleus RNA-seq of hiPSC-derived neurons from four
donors, at 0, 1 and 6 hours after stimulation. The project has two aims:

1. **Splicing changes during the stimulation response.**
2. **Genetic variants associated with splicing.**

The first two sections describe the data and what the reads contain; they
apply to both aims.

# Data

* [Data summary](data_summary.html) —
  libraries, read counts, where reads fall in the genome, donor assignment
  and processing for the three timepoints

# Annotation and read structure

* [The IsoQuant annotation, classified with SQANTI3](annotation_sqanti3.html) —
  what the transcript annotation contains, how much of it is novel, and which
  novel categories are trustworthy
* [Read structure](read_structure.html) —
  chr21: exon, intron and intergenic reads, which exons each read supports,
  and the 3' bias
* [Exon structure of reads](exon_structure.html) —
  genome-wide: how exons are extracted from the annotation, and whether each
  read's exons are consecutive, skipped or retained

# Splicing changes during stimulation

* [Junction screen and neuronal examples](splicing_candidates.html) —
  changes in splice-junction usage across 0, 1 and 6 hours, the candidate
  genes, and worked examples (CREM, TTLL7, BDNF)

# Genetic variants associated with splicing (isoLASER)

* [isoLASER setup and running notes](isolaser.html) —
  what the method does, installation, and how it is run; written before the
  first run
* [Per-donor and joint pilot on chr21](isolaser_per_donor.html) —
  why the data are split by donor, and how many events are testable at
  per-donor depth
* [Checking isoLASER variant calls against donor genotypes](isolaser_variants.html) —
  chr1 and chr10 calls compared with the imputed genotype panel, including
  heterozygous sites called homozygous at low depth
* [Genome-wide allele-specific splicing](isolaser_genome_wide.html) —
  joint analysis across chr1–22 at all three timepoints: filters, candidate
  genes, timepoint patterns and neuronal candidates; within-donor effects not
  yet confirmed
